m2-verify-default-refuse.title: Change 2 (core fix): ExternalBackend.verify() override -- default-refuse without spine evidence
m2-verify-default-refuse.imperative: In tests/test_crew_launcher.py, rewrite test_verify_result_absent_then_present_marks_completed's (~L2219) final assertion (currently `code_present == 0`) to assert REFUSE (exit 1) when verifying (neither --verify-spine nor --accept-mtime-only-risk given) a dispatch that has NO --spine and only a fresh result artifact -- name this explicitly as the single most important intentional test change in this gate. Run it via `python -m pytest tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k test_verify_result_absent_then_present_marks_completed -q` and observe it FAIL against current (pre-fix) code, which still returns 0/completed (TDD red -- attest c1, paste failure output verbatim). Then in scripts/run_crew.py add `def verify(self, entries, session, *, root, verify_spine=None, accept_mtime_only_risk=None)` as an OVERRIDE on ExternalBackend (leave CrewBackend.verify untouched) implementing exactly the handoff's verdict logic: read `spine = entry.get('spine')` and gate result_ok/present computation on `entry.get('result') is not None` (never call result_exists/result_fresh with result=None); `effective_spine = verify_spine if verify_spine is not None else spine`; if effective_spine is not None: `drove = spine_terminal(effective_spine, root)`, `entry['spine_verified'] = drove`, `fresh = drove and (result_ok if entry.get('result') is not None else True)` (AND semantics, never OR/rescue); elif accept_mtime_only_risk is not None: `entry['spine_verified'] = None`, `entry['mtime_only_risk_accepted'] = {'reason': accept_mtime_only_risk, 'at': <now ISO>}`, `fresh = result_ok`; else (default): `entry['spine_verified'] = False`, `fresh = False`. On the accept_mtime_only_risk branch reaching fresh=True, print the acceptance to BOTH stdout and stderr, including the word RISK and the reason verbatim. Set entry['result_present']/entry['result_fresh'] from whatever was actually computed (False/False when result is None). On fresh: mark completed (status/completed_at/last_heartbeat) exactly as the base class does; otherwise leave running. Save the registry, return (fresh, entry). verify_spine/accept_mtime_only_risk are not yet CLI-wired in this item (that is m4) -- call the method directly with defaults or via verify_external_result's existing call site. Run the rewritten test again and confirm PASS (TDD green -- c2, paste passing output verbatim).

m4-cli-wiring.title: Change 3: CLI wiring -- --verify-spine, --accept-mtime-only-risk, distinguishable REFUSED messages
m4-cli-wiring.imperative: In scripts/run_crew.py build_parser() (~L1901), add `--verify-spine PATH` (help: verify this checklist file reached a terminal state, checked independently of any --spine given at dispatch -- use when the crew's actual plan/spine path was only learned after it returned) and `--accept-mtime-only-risk REASON` (help: explicit, recorded override: accept a fresh result artifact alone as completion when no spine target is available to check -- required reason, printed loudly, never silent; see #432). In main()'s `args.verify_result` branch (~L1997) and in verify_external_result (~L1865), thread both new args through to ExternalBackend().verify(...) as new optional kwargs with None defaults (back-compat: verify_external_result's existing signature/callers keep working). Add the new REFUSED message, checked BEFORE falling back to the existing STALE/absent messages: compute `effective_spine_for_message = args.verify_spine or entry.get('spine')`; when `entry.get('spine_verified') is False` and effective_spine_for_message is truthy, print `REFUSED: spine <path> never reached a terminal state ...` naming the path; when `entry.get('spine_verified') is False` and effective_spine_for_message is falsy (the bare default-refuse branch, no evidence and no override), print `REFUSED: no spine evidence and no --accept-mtime-only-risk given ...` naming both flags as the way forward and citing #432. Add three new tests: test_verify_time_spine_override_completes (dispatch NO --spine; verify with --verify-spine naming a spine driven to terminal by then -- must report completed, proving the verify-time flag is consulted independently of dispatch-time state), test_verify_accept_mtime_only_risk_completes (dispatch NO --spine; verify with --accept-mtime-only-risk "reason text" and a fresh result -- must report completed; capture BOTH stdout and stderr and assert both contain the reason text and the word RISK; assert registry entry carries mtime_only_risk_accepted), test_verify_spine_only_external_dispatch_no_crash (dispatch with result=None and --spine given, spine driven to terminal -- --verify-result with no result artifact involved at all reports completed, no crash). Also, as evidence for the crash the guard prevents: run a short python -c snippet demonstrating `entry['spine']` (bracket access) raises KeyError on an entry dict built with no 'spine' key at all, contrasted with `entry.get('spine')` returning None -- paste both. Run all new tests and confirm PASS.
